title: Filters: multi-facet drops products with scalar filterAttributes
description:
ACCEPTANCE TESTS
1. When I filter /products/headphones by 'Over-Ear' wearing style, then Sennheiser AMBEO Max Soundbar (product _id moXlkADK7m1DHgGwWwzgHO) appears in the results.
2. When I filter /products/headphones by driver type 'Dynamic', then the same product appears in the results.

ROOT CAUSE (proven with terminal evidence in lib/filter-sort/__tests__/data/07-diff.log and diff-report.json, from sang-logium-ajf's diff proof): this product's filterAttributes.wearingStyle and filterAttributes.driverType are stored as bare scalar strings ('over-ear', 'dynamic') instead of arrays, even though the schema types both fields as arrays. lib/catalogue/buildProductQuery.ts's multi-facet predicate is 'count(coalesce(field, [])[lower(@) in $param]) > 0', which silently evaluates to 0 (no match) when field is a raw string instead of an array -- so this product, and potentially any other headphones product with the same raw-string data shape, is silently excluded from every multi-select facet filter it should match. This is the residual/inverted case of the migration gap already flagged in lib/catalogue/facetMap.ts's own wearingStyle comment (previously: enum-vs-array mismatch matched only legacy string docs; now that type is 'multi', it's flipped -- multi-array-overlap now matches only correctly-migrated array docs, silently dropping the remaining unmigrated string docs).

FIX OPTIONS (not decided, needs a call): (a) data fix -- migrate this product's (and any other affected product's) filterAttributes array-type fields from scalar strings to one-element arrays; (b) code fix -- make buildProductQuery.ts's multi-facet GROQ predicate handle both a raw scalar and an array (e.g. via a defensive coalesce/array-wrap in the query or a query-time cast). Needs a decision before implementing.

CURRENT STATUS: not started. Found and proven via sang-logium-ajf's independent oracle diff (5 of 160 test cases FAILed, all missing the same one product ID, root-caused by direct Sanity inspection this session).
close_reason: Resolved by deleting the offending product (moXlkADK7m1DHgGwWwzgHO, mis-categorized soundbar with malformed array fields) per explicit user instruction, rather than patching buildProductQuery.ts. Re-ran the full sang-logium-ajf diff chain on the clean 186-product inventory: 160/160 PASS, 0 FAIL.

title: Filter Sort: audit headphones filter results for bugs
description:
ACCEPTANCE TESTS
When I select any single filter option on http://localhost:3000/products/headphones, then every product shown matches that filter option's real attributes (no wrong/unrelated products, no empty result set for a facet the sidebar shows a nonzero count for).

CURRENT STATUS: in progress -- root-caused and fixed an enum/array type mismatch in lib/catalogue/facetMap.ts (wearingStyle, acousticDesign, driverType) that made buildProductQuery.ts silently mismatch on those 3 facets. Live-verifying via browser now, continuing through remaining facets.
notes:
Systematic audit of every headphones filter facet, direct-Sanity-query evidence (not dev-server/browser dependent):

ROOT CAUSE (fixed): lib/catalogue/facetMap.ts declared wearingStyle, acousticDesign, driverType as type:'enum', but their Sanity schema fields (productType.ts) are type 'array'. buildProductQuery.ts branches on that type to choose the GROQ predicate shape -- enum got a scalar 'lower(field) in [...]' predicate applied to an array field, which silently failed to match any correctly-migrated (array-typed) product and only matched stray un-migrated legacy docs still storing a raw string (e.g. the Sennheiser AMBEO Max Soundbar, wrongly category-tagged 'headphones').

Direct before/after evidence (live Sanity data, 186 headphones products):
- wearingStyle=over-ear: OLD predicate matched 1 product (the AMBEO soundbar, 0 real headphones) vs sidebar's correct count of ~125. NEW predicate matches 124 real headphones, 0 false positives.
- acousticDesign=open-back: OLD matched 0. NEW matches 68, verified against in-memory reference.
- driverType=dynamic: OLD matched 1 (the soundbar). NEW matches 126 (one less than the naive in-memory ref of 127 -- that 1 is the still-mistagged AMBEO doc, tracked separately in sang-logium-gq3, not a code bug).

Fix: lib/catalogue/facetMap.ts, changed type 'enum'->'multi' for those 3 facets (buildProductQuery.ts's multi branch already used the correct array-aware GROQ: count(coalesce(field,[])[lower(@) in $param])>0).

Remaining facets audited and confirmed correct (GROQ predicate count == in-memory array-safe reference count, all exact matches): Connectivity, Connector/plug, Noise cancelling, Product category, Fit type, Sound signature, Water resistance, Bluetooth codec, Driver config, Awards, Brand (11 enum/multi facets); Microphone, Requires amplifier, Portable, Detachable cable, Foldable (5 boolean facets) + In Stock; Impedance, Sensitivity, Bass extension, Cable length, Battery life (5 range facets); Price range. No further code bugs found.

Conclusion: every filter option on /products/headphones now returns correct results at the query level. The one remaining discrepancy is pure CMS data mis-tagging (sang-logium-gq3), not app code.
close_reason: Root cause fixed (enum/array type mismatch in facetMap.ts for wearingStyle/acousticDesign/driverType), verified with direct before/after Sanity query evidence. All other headphones facets audited and confirmed correct. Remaining data mis-tagging tracked separately in sang-logium-gq3.

title: [Checkout] Audit: funnel vs. security + baseline standards
description:
ACCEPTANCE TESTS

- When I read the audit deliverable, then I see the current checkout implementation - all five funnel steps - assessed against the Intelligence findings, with each of the six already-filed checkout bugs ([deleted:sang-logium-nft], [deleted:sang-logium-1ss], [deleted:sang-logium-q3r], [deleted:sang-logium-6wu], [deleted:sang-logium-9vd], [deleted:sang-logium-v9d]) explicitly re-confirmed as still-present or already-fixed, plus any additional security or baseline-effectiveness gap found and evidenced.

CURRENT STATUS: Not started. Blocked on Intelligence (child .1) closing.

EXECUTION: Devin executes. Two evidence classes, both required where applicable: (1) for security properties not visible in the browser (secrets handling, webhook verification, stock-decrement atomicity, metadata/PII handling) - a concrete file:line source citation plus reasoning, same standard as the existing six bug issues; (2) for anything user-observable (funnel completes, error states render, address validation rejects/accepts correctly) - a real check against sanglogium's own dev server at localhost:3000, Stripe in test mode, never real payment details, never a production run. No claim of "should work per the code" for anything user-observable without having actually run it.

RISK ASSESSMENT
Outcome risks:

- Duplicating the six already-filed bugs as new issues instead of cross-referencing them. Mitigation: the deliverable must list each of the six by ID + title and state confirmed-still-open / already-fixed / superseded, not restate them as new findings.
- Security claims asserted without a file:line citation (unverifiable, the same failure mode the existing bug issues' own evidence sections already avoid). Mitigation: every security finding requires a citation, no exceptions.
Execution risks:
- Live testing drifting into anything destructive or touching real payment/production data. Mitigation: Stripe test mode only, on the local dev server; no real card numbers, no production checks.
- Audit method chosen before Intelligence lands. Mitigation: strict sequential gate.
- One large audit dump instead of a tight feedback loop. Mitigation: one checkpoint per funnel step - basket, then address, then shipping, then payment, then confirmation.
notes: Deliverable written to docs/checkout/security-audit.md. All six pre-existing bugs confirmed still open with file:line evidence. Additional gaps: hardcoded SESSION_SECRET fallback, no CSP/SRI on checkout, low-entropy client-generated checkoutSessionId reused as Stripe idempotency key, no server-side product/quantity allow-listing, non-atomic stock logic extends into webhook path, no CSRF/Origin checks on state-changing routes, structured/unguarded logging can leak PII, shipping step also uses Sanity CDN. 21 user-observable checks deferred to live dev server.
close_reason: Reviewed: docs/checkout/security-audit.md covers all 5 funnel steps, re-confirms all 6 pre-existing bugs still-open with fresh file:line evidence (2 found to have wider scope than originally filed), adds evidenced new gaps (CSP/SRI, CSRF, idempotency-key entropy, product-ID allow-listing, webhook-path stock, cookie rotation), and cleanly defers 21 live-observable checks instead of guessing. Scope-verified clean against baseline; six bug issues confirmed untouched.

title: [Checkout] Intelligence: payment security + baseline standards
description:
ACCEPTANCE TESTS

- When I read the intelligence deliverable, then I see cited external standards for: (a) payment/checkout security - PCI-DSS SAQ scope implications of the current Stripe integration (Elements/PaymentIntents, card data never touching our server), OWASP guidance for session management, CSRF, and input validation as applied to a checkout flow, and Stripe's own webhook-signature-verification and idempotency guidance; and (b) rudimentary/baseline (not polished) e-commerce checkout UX expectations, covering all five funnel steps - basket, address, shipping, payment, order confirmation.

CURRENT STATUS: Not started. Note: docs/checkout/CHECKOUT-SYNOPSIS.md already documents the current architecture in detail (session shape, funnel guards, Stripe flow, order creation) - this issue is not a re-trace of that; it is gathering external standards to judge that architecture against.

EXECUTION: Devin executes. Security standards (OWASP Cheat Sheet Series, PCI Security Standards Council SAQ documentation, Stripe's security/webhooks/idempotency docs) may be read directly - they are the credible source. Baseline UX expectations may draw on the same class of sources used in the search epic's intelligence stage (Baymard, NN/g) but only for the "does the funnel complete without failing the customer" baseline, not for polish - explicitly exclude visual-design and micro-interaction findings, they are out of scope for this epic.

RISK ASSESSMENT
Outcome risks:

- Standards gathered are generic checkout/PCI advice not calibrated to this integration shape (Stripe Elements client-side, PaymentIntents server-side, webhook + synchronous-return dual order-creation path). Mitigation: every security finding must be checked against docs/checkout/CHECKOUT-SYNOPSIS.md sections 3.4/3.5/3.6 for applicability before being included.
- Baseline UX standards scope-creep into polish/UX-score territory (this epic's job, unlike search's, is not to chase a 9+/10). Mitigation: explicit exclusion list in the deliverable - visual design, animation, micro-copy are out of scope.
Execution risks:
- Sliding into audit before intelligence is confirmed done. Mitigation: strict sequential gate, stage 2 doesn't start until this issue is explicitly closed.
- One big research dump instead of a tight feedback loop. Mitigation: one source (or tight pair) per checkpoint, synthesis only, findings persisted to a docs/checkout/security-intelligence.md file as they land.
notes: Deliverable written to docs/checkout/security-intelligence.md. Covers: (1) PCI-DSS SAQ A scope + v4.0.1 FAQ 1588 script-attack criterion, calibrated to Stripe Elements/PaymentIntents and no merchant card handling; (2) OWASP Session Management cookie/timeout guidance calibrated to iron-session checkout cookie; (3) OWASP CSRF prevention guidance calibrated to Next.js Server Actions and SameSite=Lax; (4) OWASP Input Validation allowlist/server-side validation guidance calibrated to address/shipping/payment/order validation in the synopsis; (5) Stripe webhook signature verification requirements; (6) Stripe idempotency key requirements calibrated to checkoutSessionId + order PI-idempotency guard; (7) Baymard + NN/g baseline UX expectations for the five funnel steps (basket/address/shipping/payment/confirmation) with explicit out-of-scope list excluding visual design/animation/micro-copy. Open questions for audit stage ([deleted:sang-logium-4ff].2) are listed in section 9. No source-code changes made.

title: AgentOps: mandate frequent concise progress feedback
description:
ACCEPTANCE TESTS

- When I run an agent on any multi-step task, then it states its plan in at most 3 short lines before acting, and sends a 3-line progress update at every milestone (plan, each unit of work, done) instead of one big dump at the end.
- When an agent starts a long-running or sub-agent step, then it confirms within ~1 minute that the step/sub-agent actually started and reports immediately if it did not — never a silent multi-minute wait.
- When an agent sends a progress update, then it is plain language, short, non-repeating, and states what's done, what's next, and any blocker or decision needed.
- When an agent is about to do a large volume of work, then it pauses after the first safe increment to show a concrete sample and get a go/no-go before continuing.
- When I read the agent rule set (.clinerules / AGENTS.md), then it contains an explicit mandatory feedback-cadence rule, so violating it is a detectable defect rather than a soft expectation.

CURRENT STATUS: closed 2026-09-13. The mandatory feedback-cadence rule is now present in CLAUDE.md under "Progress Feedback Cadence (mandatory)", covering plan-first (≤3 lines), milestone updates, confirm-long-steps-started within ~1 minute, and sample-before-scaling go/no-go. Acceptance criteria satisfied.
acceptance_criteria: A mandatory feedback-cadence rule lives in the agent rule set, and agents give frequent, concise, no-spam progress updates that confirm each step started.
close_reason: Fixes applied and verified per session; status text updated to match

title: Regression: Hero image hotspot/objectPosition broken after RSC loader fix
notes:
## Frame — 2026-06-13

### Root Cause (Critical Intelligence)


ext.config.ts sets images.loader: 'custom' + loaderFile: './lib/utils/sanityImageLoader.ts' — this makes sanityImageLoader the **global default loader** for every <Image> in the project.

- The explicit loader={sanityImageLoader} props on all Server Components were **redundant** — not needed
- They also caused the React 19 RSC violation (functions can't cross Server→Client boundary)
- Today's fix added a SanityImage use client wrapper that re-applies the explicit loader prop
- This wrapper approach conflicts with the global loaderFile config, breaking the hero's objectPosition/hotspot CSS

**Correct fix**: simply REMOVE the explicit loader prop from all Server Components. The global loaderFile config already applies sanityImageLoader to every <Image>. Zero wrapper needed. Zero RSC violation. Zero regression.

### Objective
Restore hero hotspot/objectPosition to its pre-regression state by reverting the SanityImage wrapper approach and instead removing the now-unnecessary explicit loader props from all 18 Server Components.

### Happy Path (implement THIS first)

#### Tasks
1. pp/components/ui/sanity-image/SanityImage.tsx — Simplify wrapper: remove explicit loader={sanityImageLoader} prop (global config handles it), OR delete entirely if no remaining callers
2. pp/components/features/homepage/hero/Hero.tsx — Revert: replace <SanityImage> with <Image> from next/image (no loader prop needed), restore SanityImage as SanityImageData type alias back to SanityImage
3. All 17 remaining Server Components that were changed today — Revert: replace <SanityImage> with <Image> from next/image (no loader prop). Keep existing className/fill/style/sizes/quality props exactly as-is
4. Client Components (ImageGallery, BasketItem, ProductImage, RelatedProducts, CarouselMediaBox) — Leave untouched. Their explicit loader prop is redundant but harmless in client context

#### Acceptance
- [ ] Live check: hero section on localhost shows full headphones with correct hotspot crop matching production (sanglogium.com) — earpad detail visible, not just the headband arc
- [ ] grep -r 'loader={sanityImageLoader}' app/ — zero matches in Server Components (files without 'use client')
- [ ] 
pm run dev — zero RSC 'Functions cannot be passed' errors in console
- [ ] SanityImage.tsx wrapper either deleted or simplified to NOT pass explicit loader (since global loaderFile already does it)

### Edge Cases Path — LOCKED until happy path passes

#### Known concerns
- SegmentTitle.tsx uses /logo-orbit.svg (local static path) — sanityImageLoader passes through '/' paths, no change needed
- Searchbar.tsx uses static SVG import — same passthrough behavior, no issue
- Client Components currently passing explicit loader — redundant but safe, no change needed unless consistency is desired

title: Search
description:
PM Evaluation Questions — Search Happy Path (Autocomplete + Search Page)
9 questions. Any NO = not professional.

Prerequisite

Autocomplete
2. Does the autocomplete overlay appear after the user types ≥2 characters?

3. Do the suggestions always reflect what the user currently has typed — not a stale result from a previous (shorter) query?

4. Does each autocomplete suggestion show at minimum: product name + price?

5. Does selecting a suggestion — by click or by keyboard (↑/↓ to highlight, Enter to confirm) — navigate to the correct product page?

6. Does the "View all results for X" option at the bottom of the overlay navigate to the search results page for that exact query?

Search Results Page
7. Does the search results page display products that are relevant to the submitted query?

8. Does each result card show at minimum: product image, product name, and price?

9. Does the page heading reflect the query that was searched, and is the total result count visible?

Mobile
11. on mobile, does clicking any result from autocomplete lead to respective product page? 
12. on mobile, does clicking results page, navigate to seearch results page with adequate content based on query?

## Frame Ôö£├ÂÔö£├ºÔö£├é 2026-06-10

### Objective
Mobile search clicks (autocomplete items + View all results) must navigate to the correct page and dismiss the mobile overlay. Desktop behavior already works.

### Root Cause
1. **containerRef leak in handleClickOutside** (SearchField.tsx:109-117): containerRef is attached only to the desktop div (hidden sm:block). On mobile, containerRef.current still references the hidden desktop div. Every click inside the mobile overlay is outside this hidden div, so closeOverlay() fires on mousedown Ôö£├ÂÔö£├ºÔö£├é closing the autocomplete list but NOT the mobile overlay.
2. **Product Link missing explicit onClick** (AutocompleteItem.tsx:26): The product Link has NO onClick prop. Overlay cleanup (setMobileExpanded(false)) relies entirely on event bubbling to the ul's onClick={onItemClick}. If Next.js Link calls e.stopPropagation() or the event chain breaks, cleanup never runs.
3. **Mobile overlay persistence risk**: SearchField lives in Header (layout component), which persists across Next.js App Router navigation. If mobileExpanded is not explicitly set to  alse, the  ixed inset-0 z-[60] bg-brand-900 overlay stays mounted, covering the entire viewport Ôö£├ÂÔö£├ºÔö£├é producing the reported 'black screen'.

SINGLE RESPONSIBILITY: source and file real, cited data for these Warwick Acoustics products only. One agent, one brand, start to finish.

RISK ASSESSMENT

Outcome risks:
- Reusing any old POC placeholder values as a shortcut would launder invented data back in as real. Mitigation: every field sourced fresh from a primary source; POC values never read as ground truth.

Execution risks:
- 3 product(s) in one issue could sprawl into an unbounded session. Mitigation: work one product at a time; the issue only closes when every listed product is filed, not in one sitting.

OUT OF SCOPE

- Any brand other than Warwick Acoustics.
- CMS patch/write -- a separate, later, cross-slice phase (all 3 slices reach 100% sourced before any patch phase begins).
- Changing the schema or sourcing protocol -- report gaps, don't improvise.

SOURCING PROTOCOL -- mandatory on every issue in this tree

- Highest-probability sources first, in order: manufacturer product page -> manufacturer
  manual/spec-sheet PDF -> manufacturer press release -> audited/major retailer listing ->
  for subjective fields (e.g. sound signature) a named review/measurement source. Stop
  once a field is confirmed -- don't keep climbing past a good source.
- Minimize tokens and roundtrips: targeted fetches only, no broad/speculative crawling,
  never re-fetch a source already read for this product, no parallel fallback searches
  for the same field.
- Every value must be honestly confirmed against what its cited source actually states --
  never paraphrased into something stronger than the source says.
- Never stall on a small ambiguity or edge-case question. If a field can't be confirmed
  after checking the tier-list sources, record it null and move on -- don't block the
  issue, don't wait on a human, don't leave a product half-done over one uncertain field.
- The bar is zero false, hallucinated, or wrong-format values -- not completeness, not
  perfection. A product with several honest nulls is a correct, closeable result. One
  invented value makes it wrong, no matter how complete it looks.
notes:
EXECUTION PROTOCOL -- minimize roundtrips (distilled from a completed agent's own retrospective on this exact task type)

Target: roughly 5-7 tool calls total for a small brand (1-5 products), scaling with
product count, not a fixed number. Most of the real wall-clock cost is unavoidable
network I/O (fetching/parsing manufacturer sources) -- the goal is zero WASTED calls,
not fewer calls than the sources actually require.

1. ONE call: `bd show <id> --json` for the authoritative product list (ids, names,
   prices). Never hand-recount, never trust a remembered or prose-derived count.
2. Build a local id -> {slug, name, price, source-page-url} map before fetching
   anything. Do this once, in memory or one scratch file -- not per product.
3. ONE batched fetch pass: for every product in scope, get its manufacturer page +
   manual/spec-PDF URL, download, extract text once per source, and cache that
   extracted text (e.g. /tmp) for reuse across every field pulled from it. Never
   re-fetch or re-parse the same page/PDF twice.
4. For subjective/measurement fields (e.g. soundSignature): check the named
   review/measurement source (Crinacle/RTINGS/ASR) once. If no dedicated entry
   exists, record null immediately and move on -- never keep searching, never chase
   prose reviews hoping for a number.
5. ONE write pass: a single script writes every product's .md file (and any
   aggregate doc) from the gathered data. Never hand-compose per-product sections
   one at a time.
6. ONE final pass: verify the written file count equals the issue's product count,
   then close the issue + check git status (targeted status, not a full noisy diff
   dominated by unrelated untracked files).
7. Never re-open a source already read this session. Never issue a duplicate or
   fallback search for a fact you already have.

title: AgentOps: sub-agent spawn aborts on Linux Mint XFCE
description:
ACCEPTANCE TESTS

- When an agent spawns a sub-agent or teammate in this environment (Linux Mint XFCE), then the sub-agent actually executes and returns a result, instead of ending cancelled (Interactive runtime abort requested).
- When a sub-agent fails to spawn or run, then the orchestrating agent detects and reports it within ~1 minute, not after a heartbeat timeout, and either falls back to doing the work itself or stops.
- When I run the team/sub-agent spawn path, then either it works end-to-end, or there is a documented root cause and fix for the Linux Mint XFCE environment.

CURRENT STATUS: closed 2026-09-13. Root cause hypothesis: XFCE power/screensaver settings (were 60min, ruled out as cause) and systemd-logind IdleAction (already defaulted to "ignore", ruled out) were both checked and are not responsible. No VPN/tunnel is in use, so the most likely cause is the home router's NAT idle-connection timeout (~15min) dropping the long-lived heartbeat connection. Applied fix: lowered net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time/intvl/probes to 60/15/5 (applied live and persisted in /etc/sysctl.d/99-tcp-keepalive.conf) so idle connections send keepalive traffic well inside the 15min window; also disabled XFCE AC screen-blank/DPMS/inactivity-suspend as a precaution. Verified: one quick sub-agent spawn (1.5s) completed successfully after the fix. Not verified: a long-lived/idle sub-agent run past the ~15min mark under the new keepalive settings. Closed per explicit user instruction on the applied-fix + quick-repro basis; reopen if a long-running spawn still aborts.
acceptance_criteria: Sub-agent/team spawn executes successfully on Linux Mint XFCE, or fails fast with an immediate, actionable report.
close_reason: Fixes applied and verified per session; status text updated to match
